clue.text: Understanding what is the matter?

explanation.surface: Someone asks for comprehension of what the trouble is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understanding' also splits as under-standing, SUB (under) plus STANCE (standing); 'what is the matter?' reads like an enquiry about a problem but means physical stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist or meaning of something grasped is its substance, and in physics any material or stuff is a substance.

clue.text: Stars confused about what they can wear

definitions.text: Stars confused about what they can wear

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters are placed around the next word
confused tells us the letters of the word stars are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Film stars are muddled about what headgear they may put on.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars of stage and screen are the false picture; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since sun hats are what such people might wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer hats woven from dried stalks are what stars might wear on a sunny day.

clue.text: There's a clear call for it in the Services

definitions.text: There's a clear call for it in the Services

parts.words: There's a clear call for it in the Services
parts.note: reads as a demand being obvious, but describes the brass instrument that sounds clear calls in the armed forces

explanation.surface: Something is plainly in demand in the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument sounds reveille and other military signals, so a clear call is literally its job.

clue.text: Novel charm

explanation.surface: A charm that is new and original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it names Walter Scott's 1825 novel of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott wrote a crusader novel under this title, and the word itself means an amulet or lucky object.

clue.text: Tidy order by cattle head

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle or oxen
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's place names and Sheerness

explanation.surface: Instructions to tidy up given by the head of the cattle farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderliness and tidiness are the same quality, the state of being kept trim.

clue.text: Cut out for some kind of duty

explanation.surface: Someone is suited to a certain kind of obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out for' looks like 'suited to', but 'Cut out' is one definition and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove surgically is to excise, and excise is also a tax levied on goods such as alcohol.

clue.text: Out of which it's a case of sink or swim

definitions.text: Out of which it's a case of sink or swim

parts.words: Out of which it's a case of sink or swim
parts.note: in water too deep to stand in you must swim or drown

explanation.surface: Being in a situation where one either succeeds or fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of one's depth means being in water too deep to stand, hence swimming or sinking.

clue.text: An idle form of rejection

indicators.note: a form of means the words an idle are given a new shape by rearranging

explanation.surface: Rejection described as a lazy type of response.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing or turning down a request is a denial.

clue.text: Pickle not in Mrs Beeton's book

definitions.text: Pickle not in Mrs Beeton's book

parts.words: Pickle not in Mrs Beeton's book
parts.note: a pickle missing from the famous Victorian cookery book is not a relish at all but the hero of a Smollett novel

explanation.surface: A preserve that does not appear in the famous cookery book.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management is a famous Victorian British cookbook; 'Pickle' is the surname of Tobias Smollett's hero Peregrine Pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Smollett's 1751 novel The Adventures of Peregrine Pickle names its hero, whose first name fills the grid.

clue.text: Game to give one the jumps

definitions.text: Game to give one the jumps

parts.words: Game to give one the jumps
parts.note: sounds like something frightening, but describes a board game where pieces leap over each other

explanation.surface: An alarming pastime that makes one nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: In this Victorian board game, pieces move by jumping over others across the board.

clue.text: Trappings for a real GI, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that a real GI is not to be taken literally, but is to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Military kit fit for a genuine American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is an American soldier, which suits 'Trappings' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial insignia and finery, the outward trappings of rank, are regalia.

clue.text: In no position to take sides

definitions.text: In no position to take sides

parts.words: In no position to take sides
parts.note: reads as being unable to choose, but describes literally being in the middle rather than at either side

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot afford to back either party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the middle means occupying neither flank, a midpoint location.

clue.text: Would they feel out of place in the crow's-nest?

definitions.text: Would they feel out of place in the crow's-nest?

parts.words: Would they feel out of place in the crow's-nest?
parts.note: the crow's-nest is a ship's lookout, suiting the women's naval service, while small songbirds would be out of place in a crow's home

explanation.surface: Asks whether certain people would be uneasy in a ship's lookout post.
explanation.walkthrough: The WRNS (Women's Royal Naval Service) were nicknamed this, and the word also names a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the British women's naval service were known by this nickname, which is also a small songbird.

clue.text: What makes a "has-been' so attractive?

parts.note: a has-been looks like a faded celebrity, but here means anything from the past, which longing makes appealing

explanation.surface: Asks why a washed-up celebrity remains appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful longing for the past makes bygone things seem lovelier than they were.

clue.text: Value, with a twopenny increase

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny, so two of them give PP
to raise is to increase

explanation.surface: A price with a two-pence rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess the worth of something is to put a price on it.

clue.text: When such fullness causes trouble, let up one end

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of let up, one and end are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: When overeating causes discomfort, ease off at one end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When such' and 'causes' are linking words; 'trouble' rearranges LETUP + I + END.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance or completeness is plenitude.

clue.text: A row among the courtiers

indicators.note: among means the letters lie inside the run of words the courtiers

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out among royal attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level of seats rising one above another.

clue.text: No doubt they opposed the scrapping of the sovereign

definitions.text: No doubt they opposed the scrapping of the sovereign

parts.words: No doubt they opposed the scrapping of the sovereign
parts.note: scrapping the sovereign sounds like withdrawing a gold coin, but means abolishing the monarchy, which the King's supporters resisted

explanation.surface: People who objected to withdrawing a gold coin from circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also a British gold coin, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the Crown, such as the Cavaliers in the English Civil War, opposed removing the monarch.

clue.text: Settling comfortably the issue of 11

explanation.surface: Settling down cosily the offspring of some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' points to the answer at 11 across; its offspring is a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuggling down cosily is nestling, and a nestling is also a fledgling chick still in the nest.

clue.text: Highwayman has little time to right its wrong

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time
taken as written

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the word its are set in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A robber of the road soon sets right his misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highwayman' suggests a mounted robber, but a modern man on the highway drives; 'wrong' rearranges ITS into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A user of the highway today is a car driver.

clue.text: Put off building

explanation.surface: Someone postponed construction work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like 'postponed' but means cast off, as a snake its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off skin or leaves is to shed, and a shed is a simple hut or outbuilding.

clue.text: A case of getting one's own back?

definitions.text: A case of getting one's own back?

parts.words: A case of getting one's own back?
parts.note: sounds like revenge, but describes regaining something lost, or putting a case or cover on again

explanation.surface: An instance of taking revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Regaining what was lost, or getting well again, is recovery.

clue.text: Botanically Homeric at times?

parts.note: the saying that even Homer nods means the great poet sometimes dozes; a botanist's word for drooping or nodding is wanted

explanation.surface: Something in plants that resembles the epic poet now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'even Homer nods' means even the best slip up; a nodding flower is described in botany with this Latin-derived term.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists describe a drooping, nodding flower head with this term from Latin for nodding.

clue.text: Clementine's dwelling

parts.note: the folk song Oh My Darling, Clementine opens with a miner living in a cave by a canyon with his daughter

explanation.surface: The home of a girl called Clementine.
explanation.walkthrough: The American folk song begins 'In a cavern, in a canyon, excavating for a mine, dwelt a miner, forty-niner, and his daughter Clementine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song places the miner and his daughter in a large cave as their home.

clue.text: For those who want excitement

parts.note: reads like an advert for thrill seekers, but describes a drug or drink that rouses the body

explanation.surface: Something marketed to thrill seekers.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance such as caffeine that excites the nervous system is a stimulant.

clue.text: A pie's cooked brown.

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of a pie's are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pie that has baked to a brown colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'pie's' counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown pigment made from cuttlefish ink, used in old photographs, is sepia.

clue.text: Bird left by the river

parts.note: the Ouse is the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: A bird was abandoned beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like abandoned but gives L; 'by' and 'the' are links, the Ouse being a river in Yorkshire and another in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: This old name for the blackbird, also spelt ouzel, is a bird.

clue.text: Such a tonic for singers!

parts.note: tonic sounds like a pick-me-up, but tonic ... is a system of singing notes named doh, ray, me

explanation.surface: Something that refreshes vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonic sol-fa is a method of teaching sight-singing, using syllables for notes of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The note-naming syllables used to teach singing make up this system.

clue.text: The time of Wodehouse's life in The Feathers

parts.note: P. G. Wodehouse was known as Plum to his friends
an age can mean a lifetime or a time of life

explanation.surface: The best period of Wodehouse's career spent at an inn called The Feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Feathers' looks like a pub name, but is the definition; P. G. Wodehouse's nickname was Plum, and 'The time of' and 'in' are padding round the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's covering of feathers is its plumage.

clue.text: "When — hang by the wall" (LL Lost)

parts.note: a missing word from the winter song that ends Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost

explanation.surface: A gap-filling quotation from Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: LL Lost is Love's Labour's Lost; its closing song begins 'When icicles hang by the wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: The winter song pictures frozen drips of water hanging from walls in cold weather.

clue.text: He's not one to mind his own business

definitions.text: He's not one to mind his own business

parts.words: He's not one to mind his own business
parts.note: sounds like a nosy person, but describes someone who acts on behalf of another's affairs

explanation.surface: Describes a busybody who meddles.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative who handles affairs for someone else, such as a sales or estate representative, is an agent.

clue.text: Drinks that go to our heads

explanation.surface: Alcohol that makes us tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to our heads' suggests intoxication, but means being worn on the head in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A last drink before bed shares its name with the soft cap once worn in bed.
